chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'What is Islam?' He said: 'It is the religion of Allah, its name is Islam, and it was the religion of Allah before you existed, where you are, and after you. So whoever acknowledges the religion of Allah is a Muslim, and whoever acts in accordance with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded, is a believer.'

key_terms.إِسْلَام: Submission/Islam, defined here as the religion of Allah
key_terms.إِيمَان: Faith/Belief, defined here as acting upon divine commands

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Iman according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the ontological status of Islam as the primordial religion of Allah, existing independently of human creation. He establishes a crucial theological distinction: 'Islam' denotes the submission and acknowledgment of the faith, while 'Iman' (belief) is characterized by the active implementation of divine commands, reflecting the Shia understanding of the interplay between creed and action.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘What is Al-Islām?’ So Heasws said: ‘Religion of Allahazwj. It’s name is Al-Islām, and it was the Religion of Allahazwj before you happened to be, where you are, and after you. So the one who acknowledges by the Religion of Allahazwj, so he is a Muslim, and the one who acts in accordance with whatever Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Commanded with, so he is ‘Momin’ (a Believer)’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘What is Islam?’ He said, ‘It is the name of the religion of Allah. It was the religion of Allah before you were as you are now and after you it will be there. Whoever professes the religion of Allah, is a Muslim. Whoever does what Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has commanded, is a believer.’”
